result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): Both answers turn down the hero stat and big cards and propose status lanes with uniform cards. B is slightly better: it keeps the summary to a quiet strip without giving ground, keeps normal cards neutral, uses color only for exceptions, and flags a wider set of computed exceptions on the card itself. A handles fitting all trucks on screen better by sorting longest-dwell first and planning for an overflowing lane, but it suggests the over-threshold count could still be a hero element and is less clear about limiting color. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): Both answers push back on the hero stat and big cards, and both propose status lanes with same-size cards and exceptions flagged in place. B deals more concretely with fitting 40-60 trucks on one screen: it sizes lanes to peak counts, adds a two-column fallback instead of scrolling, and sorts each lane by dwell time so problem trucks come first. A's four-line cards in five lanes may not fit, and it never checks that. A is slightly stronger on keeping color for exceptions only, while B weakens its point by saying that if the user wants a hero element, it should be the over-threshold count.
